text: Face-to-face interviews at home (paper questionnaires); main questionnaire for the head of household, mini questionnaire for other members aged 12+, cultural-integration module for one child aged 15+. Turkish/Arabic translated questionnaires available for the Turkish and Moroccan groups.

Fixed question order (paper); no randomisation. Question blocks: general/household/migration, education, labour, income, health, language, group, social contacts, cultural integration, religion, imaging, family relations.
One questionnaire version per group; differences limited to the answer categories for mother tongue and ethnic subgroup.

Face-to-face (CAPI) interviews; main questionnaire (15 blocks) for heads, mini questionnaire for members aged 12+, separate health and cultural-integration blocks for the partner and one child aged 15+; Dutch, English or French.
Fixed question order; no randomisation.

Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp with TNS NIPO interviewers) with persons aged 15-64 sampled by CBS from the GBA of the 50 largest municipalities (Turks, Moroccans, Surinamese, Antilleans/Arubans, native Dutch); only the sampled person was interviewed. Fieldwork October 2004 - May 2005; corrected response 45% (Turks 47%, Moroccans 44%, Surinamese 38%, Antilleans 47%, natives 50%). An extra sample of working mothers with children under 12 was drawn in March 2005 in nine municipalities and the working partners of male Turkish, Moroccan and Antillean respondents with young children were asked a supplementary interview (47 cases; items marked '+ P' in the questionnaire, of which only dem_prtnr_flex survives as a separate variable); svy_oversample flags the resulting oversample of working men and women (228 cases).

Fixed block order A-X; no rotation or randomisation reported. Questions on the murder of Theo van Gogh were added about two weeks into the fieldwork (universe: respondents interviewed after that point).

One programmed questionnaire with group routing (INDIEN ALLOCHTOON / AUTOCHTOON / TURK, MAROKKAAN / MOSLIM / NIET IN NEDERLAND GEBOREN); the native reference sample skips the migration, language, integration and Islam blocks (.c). The time-use diary (block X) was administered by the interviewer at the end of the interview, for 'yesterday', in 72 quarter-hour slots from 06:00 to 24:00 with a 43-code activity card (tim_slot01-72, tim_act01-43; day of the week in tim_weekday, diary weights tim_wgt and tim_wgt_corr); it was skipped when the interview had run long and completed by 74% of respondents (Turks 71%, Moroccans 65%, natives 87%).

Written Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic translations (two independent translators, reconciled with SCP) supported interviews in Dutch; respondents with language problems were re-approached by 17 Turkish and Moroccan interviewers (128 interviews).

The DANS file holds the questionnaire variables, SCP constructs (societal position, earner type, labour-force status) and weights (svy_wgt, svy_wgt_grp, svy_wgt_raise); no registry linkage. The questionnaire itself is appendix 1a of the deposited fieldwork report.

Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp/TNS NIPO, with ERC interviewers for Turkish and Moroccan respondents) with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA nationwide (at least 10 addresses per municipality); a paper version existed for interviewers without a laptop. Fieldwork March 2006 - January 2007; corrected response 53% (Moroccans 50%, Turks 60%, Antilleans 54%, Surinamese 46%, natives 55%); 5,250 interviews. Part of the sample received two postage stamps with the invitation letter as an incentive experiment.
Fixed block order A-P; no rotation or randomisation reported.

Only the sampled person answered (the partner could be present). Items on Islam were routed to Muslims by the script; a respondent counted as native Dutch when both parents were born in the Netherlands. Answer cards were collected in a card booklet and read out literally. The deposited questionnaire is the CAPI script printout, which carries no variable names: items are linked to the data through the question number in the data labels and the option order of multiple-response questions.

Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic written translations (one translator, independent check); first-generation Turks and Moroccans who arrived at 15 or older were assigned to co-ethnic interviewers where possible, with gender matching.

Face-to-face CAPI interviews (Veldkamp/TNS NIPO; 243 native and 60 bilingual interviewers) with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA in two stages (municipalities, then persons): Afghans, Iraqis, Iranians, Somalis, Chinese, Poles and a native Dutch reference sample. The Polish sample was redesigned after a pilot to short-stay Poles (less than five years registered), 532 of whom completed a Polish self-completion version on the interviewer's laptop. Fieldwork February 2009 - February 2010; corrected response 43% (Iranians 44%, Iraqis 48%, Afghans 49%, Somalis 38%, Chinese 38%, Poles 42%, natives 46%); 6,911 interviews.

Fixed block order A-U; no rotation reported. One item, Q2630 (leisure-time contact with native Dutch, soc_leis_nl), was asked to a random half of the respondents with a migration background (CAPI script field exp2431 = 1); the deposit documents neither the split nor an indicator for it, so the half is visible only as .c on that variable (3,017 of 5,952 asked; the follow-up Q2640 went to both halves).

Natives skip the migration-history and civic-integration blocks (shorter questionnaire, 40 instead of 56 minutes); Chinese respondents could skip the religion items. Respondents aged 15-17 were asked to call in a parent for the household-income questions (hh_inc_band_par). The deposited questionnaire is the CAPI script printout without variable names (linked via the question numbers in the data labels).

Questionnaire, letter and folder translated into Farsi, Arabic, Dari, Somali, Chinese and Polish (DaVinci Vertalingen, checked by co-ethnic interviewers) and programmed in CAPI; short-stay respondents were approached by bilingual interviewers where possible.

Partial release: the DANS file contains only the questions listed in the deposit's READ ME (the rest is available through CBS Remote Access), and years and durations are coarsened into classes: age and partner's age in 3 classes (15-24, 25-44, 45+), length of stay 0-5/5-10/10-15/15+ years, year of marriage and of first arrival in decade bands, contractual hours in 4 classes, education in 4 classes. The IMPD keeps these as the SING-only `_cat` variants (e.g. dem_age_cat3, mig_dur_nl_cat4). The release is also statistically protected: in some variables real values are replaced by 'don't know' / 'not applicable' / 'other' codes (sex for 2 respondents, marital status 71, origin group 85 - the 'unknown' group -, generation 29 besides the natives, year of marriage 39, small categories of the household-position items recoded to 98), household size and the number of children are top-coded at 6, and the BMI is delivered in classes; the resulting .d / unknown values are protection, not non-response. The CBS microdata hold the unprotected values.

Face-to-face CAPI interviews at home (GfK with Labyrinth co-ethnic interviewers), no proxies, with persons aged 15+ sampled by CBS from the GBA stratified in six municipality strata (Turks, Moroccans, Surinamese, Antilleans/Arubans, native Dutch). Fieldwork from November 2010 for about five months; corrected response Turks 54%, Moroccans 50%, Surinamese 43%, Antilleans 48%, natives 55%; 4,125 interviews. A parallel mixed-mode experiment (web, then telephone, then face-to-face; 2,698 respondents, shortened web questionnaire) is NOT in the DANS deposit: all records have onderzoek = main study and methode = CAPI (svy_fw_phase records the two fieldwork phases, the second being a re-approach of non-respondents by another interviewer).
Fixed block order A-U; no rotation or randomisation reported. Ranking question Q1073 (fam_val_rank) asks for a 1-5 order of child-rearing values.

Group routing as in SIM 2006 (natives .c for migrant-only items; Islam items to Muslims). Partner items Q53-70, 225, 230 are proxy answers by the respondent. Respondents aged 15-17 were asked to call in a parent for the household questions (suffix _par). The deposit is statistically protected (mu-Argus on sex x 5-year age class) and version 3 removed the open-answer variables; the questionnaire is the hardcopy of the CAPI script (appendix g), which prints variable names next to the questions.

Turkish and Moroccan-Arabic translations (SIM 2006 versions reused, new items double-translated); Berber (138 interviews), Papiamento (121) and Surinamese languages (11) used orally as fallback (svy_lang_hh, svy_lang_oth). All Turkish and Moroccan respondents were interviewed by co-ethnic interviewers, Surinamese and Antilleans half by native interviewers.

Sequential mixed mode: web (CAWI) invitation first, face-to-face (CAPI) follow-up of non-respondents by bilingual interviewers (TNS NIPO and Labyrinth); CAWI and CAPI questionnaires are parallel (questionnaire_items.csv holds both; wording.csv references the CAWI version with the CAPI question id in capi_qid).

Fixed block order with randomised item order within batteries: Q801-Q815 and Q813-Q817 (opinion statements), Q895-Q89801 (opinions on NL), Q770 contact with groups and Q859-Q865 feeling thermometers (groups presented in random order, own group always last; Jews never first).
Many items asked only to respondents with a migration background (ASK ONLY IF not Q9001=7); the native reference sample gets mirrored wording ('allochtone' instead of 'autochtone' contacts).
Questionnaire available in Dutch, Turkish, Moroccan Arabic, Polish and Somali (CAWI language choice; language variable not in the public file).

CAWI (90%) with CAPI follow-up only for the Caribbean, Moroccan, Somali, Surinamese and Turkish groups (10%) because of covid; 15 CAPI interviews by video call (WhatsApp). Fieldwork 11 March 2020 - 17 January 2021 with CAPI suspended during lockdowns.

Respondents randomly assigned within origin group to A or B (svy_split). Only A: political participation (POL_4, HERK_3), institutional trust (VERTWORG), belonging (CONTACTERBIJ, ORGANBIJ), media interest and positioning (NIEUWS_3, FREQNIEU, FREQAANT, POS_4). Only B: opinion statements STELL_8_12 and STELL_1_7_5, religion items BIJBKOR and KORZELFINT, mental health items MENTALGEZ_4_4, 8_3, 8_4, BEZOEKMOG, HUISARTS, PIJN, situational discrimination DISCZELF2, Zwarte Piet items.
Fixed block order with randomised item order within batteries: Q801-Q804, Q813-Q817, Q895-Q89801, Q965-Q967.
Six script versions (svy_qversion); version differences are not documented in the fieldwork report. Early CAWI interviews ran on versions 1-3.
Dutch, Turkish, Moroccan Arabic, Polish, Somali, Farsi (svy_lang_q); a Farsi error in two items is flagged in the source (code -1).
Group terms updated: 'allochtoon' -> 'persoon met een migratieachtergrond' in most items; 'autochtone Nederlanders' retained in contact items. Text fills per group (<HERKGRP>, <LVH>).
